title: Do you love roguelikes/roguelites? Do you have 30 mins?
author: vizyn
selftext:
I'm in need of first time playtesters and would appreciate your time and effort.  Willing to swap playtests if that would be helpful to you.

[https://vizyn.itch.io/teem](https://vizyn.itch.io/teem)

I'm the solo developer of TEEM - a top-down action roguelite where you control a swarm of insects tasked with surviving a \~25-30 minute run through your choice of 5 biomes (from a pool of 11).  Each unit is a sliver of your health and a sliver of your power.  Macro decision making and micro execution are essential to a successful run.

As it stands I've had a wide range of results from first time players.  I win every run I test, but over half of my new players can't make it out of the first biome, though the sample size is small.  I could really use some fans of the genre to give it a go so I can get a better sample size/feel for the new player experience.  Balance has been tuned using my personal runs, low volume playtests, and over 10k bot runs.

**How AI was used**

I direct Claude Code (Opus 5.5) in Unity 6. Claude writes the C#, and I make the design calls and playtest. One session runs a task board and briefs the others: one takes tickets, one works on biome art. Before a change merges, a separate reviewer agent for code, gameplay, art or sound provides feedback to iterate on. I also delegate any concept design work to GPT-6 Astra.

Most of the art is Blender, built by Python scripts Claude writes and then judges from in-game screenshots and clips. Bosses, plus scenery in the biomes I haven't redone yet, are Meshy. Music and sound effects are ElevenLabs.

Bots have played over 10,000 runs for balance. They're great at catching broken cards and useless at telling me how it feels to play for the first time, which is why I'm here.
